title: FastAPI introduction: HTTP and APIs

spans.text: WHY USE THIS?
FastAPI builds JSON APIs that web and mobile applications call over HTTP; type annotations help validate inputs and describe the API contract.
PURPOSE AND REAL-WORLD USE

FastAPI is an ASGI web framework that uses Python types. We define HTTP endpoints; browsers, phones, and other services call them to receive or send JSON. This lesson introduces the server, a route, and how to run it.

To run these examples locally, install `pip install fastapi uvicorn httpx` plus any extra package named in the lesson. Save the server example as `app.py` and start `uvicorn app:app --reload`. `--reload` is for development only.

WHERE DOES THIS APPEAR IN REAL LIFE?
For example, a mobile app can call `/health` to check whether a service is running.
If this part is omitted: Without a FastAPI app and route decorator, there is no endpoint for an ASGI server to call; an ordinary Python function is not a network API.

REQUEST AND EXPECTED RESPONSE

LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import FastAPI` — Imports FastAPI so the program can create its application object; without it, `FastAPI` is undefined.
`app = FastAPI(title="Study API")` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`@app.get("/health")` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`async def health_check():` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`return {"status": "ok"}` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.
PRACTICE: CHECK IT WITH AN HTTP CLIENT
This complete file calls the app locally with TestClient; it does not open a server port. Install `httpx` for TestClient.
COMPLETE RUNNABLE CLIENT TEST
QUESTION: What will this code print? Predict first, then run it.

spans.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI(title="Study API")

@app.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    return {"status": "ok"}

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

with TestClient(app) as client:
    response = client.get("/health")
    print(response.status_code, response.json())

spans.text: EXPECTED CLIENT-TEST OUTPUT

LINE-BY-LINE CODE EXPLANATION
`from fastapi import FastAPI` — Imports FastAPI so the program can create its application object; without it, `FastAPI` is undefined.
`app = FastAPI(title="Study API")` — `FastAPI()` creates the ASGI application that holds the routes and is passed to the server.
`@app.get("/health")` — Binds an HTTP method and URL path to this function; without the decorator, it is not an API endpoint.
`async def health_check():` — Defines the endpoint the server calls; parameter names help bind path, query, or body data.
`return {"status": "ok"}` — Returns the HTTP response value; FastAPI converts it to JSON and applies the response model.
`from fastapi.testclient import TestClient` — Imports TestClient so an HTTP request can exercise the app without opening a server port.
`with TestClient(app) as client:` — Creates a test HTTP client for the app and closes it when the context ends.
`response = client.get("/health")` — Sends the stated GET request through the test client and stores the response.
`print(response.status_code, response.json())` — Reads and prints both the HTTP status code and parsed JSON response.
COMMON MISTAKES
Confusing a started server with a successful endpoint call: startup only makes the server ready to receive requests.

spans.title: Practical tip
spans.text: For a first check, open `/docs` in a browser; FastAPI serves interactive OpenAPI documentation.

spans.title: One level deeper
spans.text: An ASGI server such as Uvicorn handles HTTP connections; FastAPI maps a request to an endpoint function. They have different jobs.

spans.title: Important warning
spans.text: This example is for local learning. Do not leave debug features enabled in production; configure security controls separately.
RUN IT LOCALLY
Run `pip install fastapi uvicorn`, save this as `app.py`, then start `uvicorn app:app --reload`. Call the endpoint in `/docs`. `--reload` is for local development only.
